newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty just below NBP-guarded levels, depos flat.
newsitem.headline: Zloty just below NBP-guarded levels, depos flat.

text.p: The early Polish zloty kept its head down just below the central bank patrolled level of 2.5 percent from parity, but dealers said it might inch higher later today provoking an intervention against it.

They said the potential rise of the zloty, which has been repeatedly punished by the central bank for the last four days, could be fuelled by domestic players cutting currency exposure to keep higher yielding zlotys over the weekend.
"Early trade might be a waiting game with the National Bank of Poland, but I have a feeling that in the afternoon the NBP might be active again," said Jerzy Wyjadlowski of Bank Slaski.

At 0800 GMT the zloty was at 2.50/2.47 percent from the trading band centre against 2.51/2.44 percent at opening. On Tuesday the NBP stepped in against the Polish unit as soon as it reached 2.51 percent from parity.
The zloty was at 3.1410/20 against the dollar, from 3.1400/15 at opening and at 1.8330/41 against the mark from 1.8333/50 at opening.
Dealers said foreign investors may play a lesser role on the forex market today as there were virtually no offers of treasuries on the secondary market after the rampant buying in the last four days.
"Foreigners are not present on the market at the moment because there are no more treasuries to buy," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, T-bill and bond dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

Despite monthly tax payments and a net outflow of 1.18 billion zlotys from the system today the money market was highly overliquid and banks expected the NBP to stage a 700 million reverse repo to clear the excess cash.
Overnight deposits were quoted at 19.50/20.30 percent against 19.50/20.50 percent at opening with tomorrow next cash at 19.40/20.40 percent.
